name: AZERTY Global
description: Complete OKLM description of the AZERTY Global layout (49 graphic keys, 8 ISO levels, 29 dead keys), generated from the azerty.global web tester data and verified field-by-field against it. Frame keys (function row, navigation, numpad) are out of the draft 0.1 core.

conformance.scope: Key reference grid used for canonical key identifiers.

metadata.description: Generated from the AZERTY Global source of truth (azerty.global site data). The site data remains the authoritative source for the layout.

OKLM_siteView._lisezmoi: Ce que la vue data/AZERTY Global.json porte et que le coeur OKLM 0.1 ne modelise pas : prose editoriale, groupement en rangees, correspondance materielle (scancode, code virtuel) et exemples des touches mortes. Le reste de la vue est genere depuis le coeur du manifeste.

philosophy.ambition: Become the new French AZERTY standard across all operating systems, replacing AZERTY AFNOR within 5 years
target_audience: French-speaking general public and writers needing proper French typography (goal: millions of users)
Developers needing easy access to programming symbols
Anyone typing in European languages (foreign residents in France, French speakers learning languages)
design_principles: Minimal changes from classic Windows AZERTY: fix flaws without revolution
Smart Caps Lock that only affects letters, with easy access to É, È, Ç, À
Programming symbols on AltGr home row ({ } [ ] | \)
Full support for French and European languages
Intuitive placement: no stickers needed, easy to remember
Sparse AltGr layer to limit Ctrl+Alt conflicts; rare characters via dead keys
not_goals: Radical ergonomic optimization (this is not a Bépo or Dvorak)
Compatibility with the AFNOR NF Z71-300 standard

changes_from_traditional_azerty.Period and semicolon swapped on B08: Period is more frequent than semicolon
changes_from_traditional_azerty.Smart Caps Lock: only affects letters: Easy access to É, È, Ç, À without Shift
changes_from_traditional_azerty.@ and # on E00: Copies Mac AZERTY, @ much more accessible for emails
changes_from_traditional_azerty.ù and % moved to place acute and grave a: Direct access to very common European accents
changes_from_traditional_azerty.µ, § and ¤ become dead keys for Greek al: Access to many more characters via these dead keys

conventions.caps_lock_behavior: Caps Lock only affects keys that produce letters (accented or not)
conventions.caps: If absent, use the base value (Caps lock does not affect symbols)
conventions.caps_shift: If absent, use the shift value (Caps lock does not affect symbols)
conventions.caps_alt_gr: If absent, use the alt_gr value (Caps Lock does not affect symbols)
conventions.caps_shift_alt_gr: If absent, use the shift_alt_gr value (Caps Lock does not affect symbols)
conventions.null_meaning: No output for this key combination

design_notes: Shortcuts for frequent letters with secondary diacritics: Polish (ę ł ż ą), Czech (č š), Romanian (ă ș), Spanish & Portuguese (ñ ã)
Quick uppercase for French accented letters: é/è/ç/à → É/È/Ç/À
Shortcuts for frequent letters with secondary diacritics: French (ù), Turkish (ş ğ ı), Nordic (ø å), other (ə)
